partial_progress.details: Phases 6-8 are COMPLETED, committed, and verified (phases 1-5 landed in prior dispatches). Phase 6 replaced test-lint-shellcheck-parallel.sh's ~120s real-corpus acceptance pair with a fast, deterministic fixture-based dispatch-shape proof (~2s) and closed the suite's hint-coverage gap; it also found and fixed an unrelated latent bug (test-check-record-versioning.sh had never had its executable bit set, so run-all.sh had silently SKIPPED it, never executed it, since it was added). Phase 7 made --skip-unchanged structurally unreachable from deploy_findings_snapshot (the single shared function behind every pre/post findings-baseline comparison in the codebase), closing the dispatch's own named sharpest correctness hazard, and added interface-level proof of all three fail-open classes (unreadable store, sentinel key, format_version mismatch). Phase 8 measured both verify-deploy-testing suites' nested-invocation costs, then narrowed one (test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh's baseline: 159.2s -> 25.2s, an 84% cut) and split the other's non-narrowable 23-gate crash net into its own suite (test-verify-deploy-gate-selection-crash-net.sh) for scheduling rather than cost reduction. Five phases remain (9-13); Phase 9 (per-gate equivalence/seeded-violation proof) is explicitly flagged in this dispatch's own Phase 8 handoff as plausibly a multi-dispatch phase on its own. Mid-task source-vs-deployed drift (expected, since this task's own source-store edits have not yet been redeployed -- that is Phase 13's job) is producing two pre-existing-looking failures in test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh; logged, not fixed, expected to resolve at Phase 13's redeploy.

memory_candidates.content: guard-destructive-git.sh (the PreToolUse hook that refuses `git add -A`/`--all`/a bare directory pathspec on a dirty tree) is a PURE COMMAND-TEXT match with no cwd-awareness: it refuses these forms inside ANY git repository the Bash tool targets, including a throwaway /tmp scratch repo created solely for test-fixture measurement and unrelated to the project it is guarding. There is no exemption for a disposable repo. Workaround: build an explicit file list and pass it to `git add --` (e.g. `mapfile -d '' files < <(find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' -print0); printf '%s\0' "${files[@]}" | xargs -0 git add --`), which the guard accepts since it is an explicit pathspec, not a directory/glob/`-A` form.

validate-bounded-waiter.sh (the PreToolUse hook enforcing the PID-liveness-not-process-name-match rule for build/CI waits) blocks ANY Bash-tool command combining a `kill -0 PID` loop with `pgrep -f`/`ps | grep`, even when the process-name match is used purely for passive SAMPLING/counting (e.g. measuring peak concurrent worker-process count during a test) rather than as the loop's actual liveness/exit condition. The hook cannot distinguish intent from the command text alone. When you need to observe concurrent-process behavior deterministically (e.g. proving a worker-pool cap is honored), do not reach for live `pgrep`/`ps` polling at all -- instead substitute a PATH-prioritized stub binary for the real tool under test that self-logs start/end timestamps (and its own argv) to a file, then compute peak concurrency, invocation count, and per-invocation argument shape from that log AFTER the run completes. This is also faster and more deterministic than real-tool timing (no real work is done, so a short fixed `sleep` in the stub gives a wide, host-load-independent timing margin).

When a cache/content-digest library resolves file paths against a caller-supplied TARGET root (not the invoking process's own source location), a test fixture built as a bare rsync'd copy with no sibling `verify-deploy.sh`/registry/library files at the expected relative path will make every composite-key computation silently fall through to the library's own 'cannot compute' sentinel -- no cache entry is ever written, and a test designed to corrupt/exercise that cache entry has nothing to act on. Symptom: a 'control' case that warms a cache entry and expects a subsequent run to skip/hit finds no entry file at all. Fix: symlink the real source tree (or otherwise make the implementation-resolvable files reachable) into the scratch target at the exact relative path the library expects, while keeping the fixture's own CORPUS content scratch-local and isolated. Always add a 'control' case (a genuinely matching entry DOES skip/hit) before trusting any 'negative' case (a corrupted entry does NOT skip/hit) in this kind of cache-fixture test -- a broken fixture and a correctly-fail-open library produce the identical observable result (no skip), so the negative cases alone cannot distinguish 'the feature is safe' from 'the harness never actually exercised the skip path'.
